title: Dashboard date presets: read the spec macro window table instead of a second table with different spellings
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

Filed by the record-page epic seat under epic #26676. An independent reviewer assessed this and the seat re-read the evidence. The maintainer: 「三点都按 A：相对日期立独立卡，在 #28971 第一版立卡前合入，包含早于/晚于的相对点；仪表盘拼法另立低优先级卡；两只钟另立 finding。」 (2026-11-02). Code readings below are on `main` `a4015ab47b`. No `domain:*` label is set: triage routes this card.

The maintainer asked for this as low priority.

## Reading

The same 13 presets have two tables:

- `packages/spec/src/data/date-range-presets.ts:120-136`, `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS`: `this_week: ['{week_start}', '{week_end}']`.
- `ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts:165-179`, `PRESET_RANGES`: `this_week: { from: '{current_week_start}', to: '{current_week_end}' }`. Month, quarter and year differ the same way.

Both spellings resolve today, as aliases (`DATE_MACRO_ALIAS_TOKENS`, `packages/spec/src/data/date-macros.zod.ts:118`). On the preview, `between` with `{month_*}` and with `{current_month_*}` returned the same rows. So nothing is wrong on screen; the risk is the two tables drifting.

## Target

`dashboard-filters.ts` derives its preset bounds from the spec's table, with no second table. Behaviour is unchanged. No new key or option.

## Acceptance

- `PRESET_RANGES` is gone, or built from `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS`.
- All 13 dashboard presets return the same rows as before.
- A stored dashboard config that uses the `{current_*}` spelling still works.
